dataScale.name: occupancy
dataScale.purpose: Ordinal olive-to-lime scale; lightness and chroma rise together. On the light land data-1 (6.5:1) and data-2 (3.8:1) hold by themselves and the lighter two do not, so every mark of the scale wears an ink ring (The Ring Rule: occ-ring inside a drawn area, the lighter dot-ring outside). A listing with no figure is not on the scale: an empty dot-none ring, "No figure" in the key.

display.purpose: The first screen's headline only, three lines, 500 at -0.035em; sized so the longest line fits the 42% column, at most 64px. Each line rises out of a mask at its own foot in the opening.

headline.purpose: --th-heading: a product's name beside its icon, "How the numbers are made.", "Ask the team." 36px on a phone to 44px from 1440px, weight 500.

figure-large.purpose: --th-text-figure: the tipping point and the counts the database holds; 400, tabular, -0.04em (-0.03em on the How counts). Never counted up.

statement.purpose: --th-text-statement: a product's claim under its name, the panels' opening sentence, the hero's sentence.

lede-large.purpose: --th-text-lead: the verdict (500), a report page's title, a stop's name on the How line, the titles inside a card.

title.purpose: A title inside a card or a stop on the How line, at 500 (600 on the How line).

body.purpose: --th-text-body: running text in full ink, the search field's text, list rows, the chat bubbles, and every action at 600.

small.purpose: --th-text-small: captions, notes, the report's running head, the cards pinned on the map, the curve's caption.

fine.purpose: --th-text-fine: the floor. Chart ticks, the hero's strip (pause, next town, the town's name, the key, the Demo data tag) and the map credit, tags, the occupancy label on a pinned card.

action.purpose: The label of every filled button (action, solid, paper) and text button: body size at 600.

wordmark.purpose: Plotsights beside its drawn "o" in the nav: 600 (--th-wordmark-weight), one step above display so the name holds.

shadows.name: shadow-color
shadows.purpose: --th-shadow: the one shadow colour on paper, ink at 35%.

shadows.name: pinned-on-map
shadows.purpose: An area's figures (a white card) floating on the light map; it also carries a 1px border of ink at 24%.

shadows.name: place-list
shadows.value: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, #1C2116 24%, transparent), 0 18px 36px -18px color-mix(in srgb, #1C2116 45%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: The list of places that opens under the search field and floats over the page.

shadows.name: report-sheet
shadows.purpose: The report's sheet, an object lying on its white panel.

shadows.name: field-edge
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: the search field's 1px ink edge (60% on hover), drawn as a spread shadow.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: --th-ease: the one exponential ease-out, for every transform and every authored moment.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Fill changes on hover and the 0.97 press of a filled button; the arrow inside moves 3px over 0.2s.

motion.name: opening-line-rise
motion.purpose: The opening (first page of a visit only, never with reduced motion): each of the headline's three lines rises from translateY with a clip-path mask at its own foot (Opening.tsx). The name's two halves rise first (0.42s, 0.08s apart) and the plot's line draws from 0.62s for 0.82s.

motion.name: tour-pin
motion.purpose: A pinned card arriving beside its drawn area; corners drop in 0.35s; the area traces corner by corner. One town leaves west as the next comes from the east (opacity 0.9s, a 3% slide over 1.2s).

motion.name: stream-word
motion.purpose: The Connector's answer streams word by word; how firm it is, its date and its link follow at words x 34ms + 260ms. Every word is in the page from the start; only opacity waits.

motion.name: page-turn
motion.purpose: A report page turn (ps-leaf-out / ps-leaf-in; LEAF_MS 250), set off by the rail, the pager, arrow keys on the sheet, or a sideways swipe of 48px.

motion.name: sheet-deal
motion.purpose: The report's sheet laid on its panel when the panel first arrives.

motion.name: how-line-fill
motion.value: animation-timeline: view(); linear, ranges cover 10% to 41% across, cover 35% to 60% down
motion.purpose: How the numbers are made: the rail fills with olive and each stop it reaches turns olive as the line is scrolled through (CSS scroll-driven animations only; across from 1100px, down below). Without scroll timelines or with reduced motion the line is simply drawn.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No opening, no tour, no streaming, no scroll fill, no page slide: everything in its final state.

breakpoints.name: search-arrow-only
breakpoints.value: (max-width: 479px), (min-width: 1024px) and (max-width: 1179px): the search button is its arrow alone

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.value: 1024px (words on the left, the frameless map over the right 58%, faded; panels go two-column)

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.value: 1280px (the strip's key names its season, "short-lets this season")

breakpoints.name: page-max
breakpoints.value: 1440px (64px gutters; headline and heading at their largest)

narrative.overview:
The page is paper and ink, measured and quiet, in the manner of the data products the owner takes as his anchor (PriceLabs for type and wording) and of those that use olive and lime seriously (Sylvera's deep-green band with lime as a data series; Wise and Ramp, where lime is one sharp signal and never the ground). Beside the words, the product's own map of a real Cyprus town comes out of the paper, and every short-let on it is a point whose colour says how booked it has been this season, from a dull olive to lime, each inside a fine ink ring. That map is the page's one rich thing. Everything else gives it room: one face, one ink, an olive action, white sheets on paper, hairlines where a table or list needs them, and no ornament.

The idea, in the subject's own terms: **on this page, every listing the team reads becomes a point on the town's map, and lime is what the market looks like where it is fullest.** Lime has one meaning wherever it appears: the top of the occupancy scale, which on the panels is the side of the tipping point where a short-let out-earns a tenant.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground (`#F5F4EE`), olive-black ink, an olive action; no tinted washes behind sections.
The light map of a real town, frameless, fading into the paper; the Playground's curve and the Connector's map answer sit on the same light land.
Deep olive only at the page's end: the close and the footer.
An olive-to-lime data scale, monotone in lightness, where lime is only ever data.
Google Sans at 500 for display and 400 for large figures; nothing heavier than 600.
Line icons with one lime fill inside an ink line.
Opaque glass for the surfaces (nav, search, the cards on the map, the product panels, How's listing card): 78% white, a 24px blur, a light rim; one soft shadow only on what is raised.

rules.name: Lime Means Data
rules.body: Lime marks how full a listing is, at the top of the scale, and nothing else. It is never a ground, a button, a link, a headline word or an ornament (the owner rejected "forest + lime" as a ground swap on 2026-10-08).

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: On a light ground a mark of the scale always sits inside a ring of ink (`occ-ring`, or `dot-ring` for the listings outside the drawn areas): a listing's dot, the key's swatches, a lime square, an icon's fill.

rules.name: Deep Olive Ends the Page
rules.body: Deep olive is the close and the footer and nothing else. A section never opens on it, and the page is never dark.

rules.name: Nothing Under the Words
rules.body: The map fades to nothing before the words' column ends, so every text token keeps its contrast against the worst pixel behind it; no listing, area or card is drawn there.

rules.name: The Olive Works
rules.body: Olive is for what the visitor does and for the brand (the action, the drawn corners, the name); the scale is for what is counted. Neither does the other's job.

rules.name: The Turned Over Rule
rules.body: The close is the paper's words on deep olive, not a second palette; the focus ring inverts with it.

rules.name: One Face Rule
rules.body: Google Sans for everything; range comes from size and two weights, never a second family.

rules.name: The Floor
rules.body: 15px is the smallest text on the page.

rules.name: Figures Are Regular
rules.body: A large figure is 400 with tabular numerals; weight is for labels.

rules.name: The Glass Rule
rules.body:
The owner, 2026-10-14: "bring glass back. I like opaque glassomorphism for the most parts of the website". Professional, not consumer:
- **Where:** the nav once scrolled (the paper at 84%), the search field and its list, the cards pinned on the map, the three product panels, How's example listing card. Everything else is solid: every button (one flat fill), the deep-olive close and footer, and anything inside a glass panel (the report's sheet and the chat bubbles take the same rim and edge on solid white: a blur inside a blurred panel only sees that panel).
- **What:** 78% white, `blur(24px) saturate(1.4)`, a 1px light rim inside, a 1px ink edge at 12% (the search field keeps a 34% edge, which a control needs to be found). No coloured glass, no rainbow rim, no glow, no beaded buttons.
- **Something behind it:** glass shows only where there is something to blur: the map behind the hero's cards; behind the product panels the island's own map at half strength (`.ps-panels::before`), static, which no loose text sits on. How's card lies on paper and reads as a nearly white card.
- **Text holds:** measured against the worst pixel behind every text element on the panels (desktop and phone), every token keeps or betters its contrast on the paper (muted 7.06 → 7.42, ink 14.91 → 15.6): the glass is lighter than the paper.
- **Cost and fallbacks:** about five blurred layers on a screen at most (nav, a panel or two, the cards); no glass in glass. Without `backdrop-filter`, or with `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce`, every surface is its solid fill and the backdrop map is not drawn.

dos: Keep the page paper; let the faded map be the rich thing.
Put lime only on data, and ring it in ink on a light ground.
Set large figures at 400 and display at 500.
Show all three markets wherever an area is summed up ("don't mislead the customer", owner, 2026-10-09), and say what every figure covers.
Give each section one working thing built from real data, usable with a thumb and readable without its script.
donts: Don't make lime a ground, a button, a link or a headline word.
Don't wash a section in a tint, and don't put anything but the close and the footer on deep olive.
Don't let the map, a listing, an area or a card under the words.
Don't use pills, eyebrows, monospace labels, logo tiles, coloured or beaded glass, glass inside glass, gradients as decoration or shadows at rest.
Don't count figures up, or hide content until a scroll or a script.
open: **The opening:** two further ideas were storyboarded on 2026-10-14 (the plot leaving the name to become the first area; the listings lighting from the name's side); neither is built.
**The Playground** (`/dashboard`) is not yet on G.
